chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنِ الْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: إِنَّ ثَوْرًا ثَارَ بِالْكُوفَةِ فَثَارَ إِلَيْهِ النَّاسُ بِأَسْيَافِهِمْ فَضَرَبُوهُ وَ أَتَوْا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَسَأَلُوهُ

translations.en: A bull became wild in Kufah, so the people rushed against it with their swords and struck it. Then they came to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام and asked him about it.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ ذَكَاةٌ وَحِيَّةٌ وَ لَحْمُهُ حَلَالٌ

translations.en: So he said: "It is a valid slaughtering while alive, and its meat is halal (permissible)."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an animal that became uncontrollable and was struck down by people with their swords. Imam Abu Abdillah عليه السلام relates that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام judged such killing to count as valid slaughtering, making the meat halal (permissible).
en.seo_question: Is the meat of a wild or uncontrollable bull halal (permissible) if it is struck with swords before formal slaughter?

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, Imam 'Ali عليه السلام
